items.title: Phase 1 Trial of INR731 for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This early-stage trial is testing a new drug called INR731, either alone or combined with standard hormone therapies (ARPIs), in men with metastatic prostate cancer. The study aims to determine safe dosing and how well the drug is tolerated. Early results will assess if the drug shows promise in slowing cancer growth.

items.title: Phase 3 Trial: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This large phase 3 trial compares enzalutamide (standard hormone therapy) alone versus combined with mevrometostat, a new investigational drug. The study enrolls men with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer who have not received prior hormone therapy or chemotherapy. Results could establish a new treatment combination for newly diagnosed metastatic disease.

items.title: Phase 2 Trial: Olaparib With or Without Cediranib for mCRPC
items.summary: This trial tests whether adding cediranib (a drug that blocks blood vessel growth) to olaparib (a PARP inhibitor) improves outcomes compared to olaparib alone in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. PARP inhibitors target cancer cells with DNA repair defects. The trial is no longer enrolling new patients.

items.title: Phase 3 Trial: AZD2265 Versus Standard Care for PSMA-Positive mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares AZD2265, a new PSMA-targeted drug, to standard treatments in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer whose tumors express PSMA. The study measures how long patients live without cancer progression and overall survival. PSMA is a protein commonly found on prostate cancer cells.

items.title: Phase 2 Trial: Radiation Plus Darolutamide for Oligoprogressive mCRPC
items.summary: This pilot trial tests stereotactic radiation (SBRT) combined with darolutamide hormone therapy in men with castration-resistant prostate cancer that is progressing in just a few spots (oligoprogression). The goal is to delay the need for more intensive systemic chemotherapy by targeting limited disease sites with focused radiation.

items.title: Study: PSMA PET Predictors in High-Risk Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Czech study identifies which standard lab tests and clinical factors predict when PSMA PET scans will find metastases in newly diagnosed high-risk prostate cancer patients. Researchers aim to help doctors decide which patients most need advanced PSMA imaging. PSMA PET is more sensitive than traditional CT and bone scans for detecting spread.

items.title: Phase 3 Trial: Saruparib Plus Hormones for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial tests saruparib (a PARP inhibitor) combined with standard hormone therapy versus hormone therapy alone in men with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer. The study measures time to cancer progression on scans. PARP inhibitors work particularly well in cancers with DNA repair gene mutations.

items.title: Phase 2 Trial: Zanzalintinib for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This upcoming trial will test zanzalintinib, a drug that blocks multiple growth signals in cancer cells, in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study focuses on patients whose cancer has spread to soft tissues or organs. Early data suggests this drug may be effective in previously treated mCRPC.

items.title: Phase 2 Trial: Nivolumab Plus Docetaxel for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This trial combines immunotherapy (nivolumab), chemotherapy (docetaxel), and hormone therapy in men with newly metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer who have specific genetic mutations (DNA damage repair defects) or immune-active tumors. The combination aims to boost the immune system's ability to fight cancer while chemotherapy weakens tumor cells.

items.title: Phase 3 Trial: Lu-177-PSMA Plus Hormones for Newly Metastatic Disease
items.summary: This major phase 3 trial tests whether adding Lu-177-PSMA radioligand therapy to standard hormone treatment improves outcomes in men with newly diagnosed metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. Lu-177-PSMA delivers targeted radiation directly to cancer cells expressing PSMA protein. Over 1,100 patients enrolled; no longer accepting new participants.

items.title: Phase 3 Trial: Pluvicto for Oligometastatic Prostate Cancer After Surgery
items.summary: This trial tests lutetium-177 vipivotide tetraxetan (Pluvicto) versus observation in men with oligometastatic prostate cancer (limited spread) after initial surgery or radiation. The goal is to determine if targeted radioligand therapy can control early recurrence and delay the need for hormone therapy, preserving quality of life.

items.title: Phase 2/3 Trial: AAA817 After Lu-177-PSMA Progression
items.summary: This trial tests AAA817, a next-generation PSMA-targeted therapy, in men whose castration-resistant prostate cancer progressed after treatment with Lu-177-PSMA radioligand therapy. The study compares AAA817 to standard chemotherapy options. This addresses an important unmet need for patients who have exhausted PSMA radioligand options.

items.title: Phase 1/2 Trial: PDS01ADC Combinations for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This trial tests PDS01ADC, an antibody-drug conjugate (a targeted therapy that delivers chemotherapy directly to cancer cells), combined with standard treatments for both castration-sensitive and castration-resistant metastatic prostate cancer. The study evaluates safety and effectiveness of this novel drug class in multiple treatment settings.

items.title: Phase 2 Trial: Lutetium Lu-177 Dotatate for Neuroendocrine Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This trial tests lutetium Lu-177 dotatate, a radioactive drug approved for other neuroendocrine tumors, in men with metastatic prostate cancer showing neuroendocrine features. These are aggressive cancers where some cells produce hormones. The drug targets somatostatin receptors found on these cells and delivers targeted radiation.

items.title: Phase 3 Trial: 177Lu-TLX591 Plus Standard Care for mCRPC
items.summary: This global phase 3 trial compares 177Lu-TLX591 (another PSMA-targeted radioligand therapy) plus standard care versus standard care alone in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer previously treated with hormone therapy. The study evaluates if adding this targeted radiation improves survival and disease control.

items.title: Phase 3 Trial: Opevesostat After First Hormone Therapy Failure
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares opevesostat (a new drug class) to switching to a different hormone therapy in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer whose disease progressed on one hormone treatment. The study includes patients with and without specific AR gene mutations. Results could provide a new treatment option after first hormone therapy failure.

items.title: Phase 1 Trial: Actinium-225 Therapy for mCRPC
items.summary: This early trial tests [225Ac]Ac-FL-020, a radioligand therapy using actinium-225 (a different radioactive element than lutetium-177), in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Actinium-225 delivers more powerful alpha radiation over shorter distances, potentially killing cancer cells more effectively. The study evaluates safety and dosing.

items.title: Research: IL-12 Enhanced PSMA CAR-T Cells for Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: Researchers developed improved CAR-T cell therapy targeting PSMA for advanced prostate cancer. The new design uses human-derived antibody fragments and adds IL-12, a molecule that boosts T cell activity. Lab and animal studies show enhanced cancer-killing ability with increased T cell expansion and immune activation, addressing prior safety concerns with earlier versions.

items.title: Clinical Review: Optimizing Care for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.source: American Society of Clinical Oncology educational book. American Society of Clinical Oncology. Annual Meeting
items.summary: This educational review provides doctors with a framework for managing metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. It covers sequencing multiple treatment types including hormone therapies, chemotherapy, PARP inhibitors, and radioligand therapy. The review emphasizes personalized treatment selection based on molecular testing, imaging findings, and patient-specific factors.

items.title: Review: New Therapies Beyond Hormone Treatment for mCRPC
items.summary: This comprehensive review discusses emerging treatment strategies for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer beyond standard hormone therapies. It covers PARP inhibitors for DNA repair defects, PSMA radioligand therapy, bispecific antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates, and immunotherapy. The review highlights how molecular testing can guide treatment selection for these newer options.

items.title: Meta-Analysis: Prognostic Factors for PSMA Radioligand Therapy Outcomes
items.summary: This comprehensive analysis of multiple studies identifies which patient and disease factors predict better or worse outcomes with PSMA-targeted radioligand therapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Understanding these prognostic factors helps doctors identify which patients are most likely to benefit from this treatment and counsel them appropriately about expected outcomes.

items.title: Review: Combination Strategies to Overcome PARP Inhibitor Resistance
items.summary: This review examines how to overcome resistance to PARP inhibitors in cancer treatment, including prostate cancer. It discusses combining PARP inhibitors with other drugs like immunotherapy, hormone therapies, or targeted agents. The article addresses why resistance develops and how rational drug combinations may improve long-term responses beyond single-agent PARP inhibitor therapy.

items.title: Research: Dual BRD4/AKT Inhibitor for Resistant Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: Scientists developed a new drug that simultaneously blocks two cancer growth pathways (BRD4 and AKT) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. This dual approach targets resistance mechanisms driven by the c-MYC gene that often emerge when treating with single-pathway inhibitors. Lab studies show the compound overcomes drug resistance better than single-target treatments.
